question.text: The Contras were from this Central American country.
question.clue: In the 1990's, this country's rule passed from the FSLN to the opposition led by Violeta de Chamorro.

swap.leadin: Name these Latin American nations that were the site of twentieth-century violence.
swap.text: A CIA-backed 1973 coup in this nation led to the suicide of president Salvador Allende in Santiago's La Moneda Palace.
swap.clue: A longtime dictator of this country employed the Chicago Boys as economic advisors.

question.leadin: Smaller islands off the coast of this island include Gonˆave [go-nahv] Island near Port-au-Prince and Tortuga off the northern coast.
question.text: Name this island whose land is divided between two modern countries.
question.clue: An independence movement on this island called La Trinitaria was led by Juan Pablo Duarte.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about self-declared monarchs.
swap.text: In 1804, Jean-Jacques Dessallines declared himself the emperor of this country. This country was once the colony of Saint-Domingue, but it gained independence in a slave revolt against France led by Toussaint L'Overture.
swap.clue: This country and the U.S. Still dispute who controls Navassa Island.

question.leadin: The death of President Francisco Solano Lopez marked the end of this war.
question.text: Name this destructive South American conflict in which a namesake coalition crushed Paraguay and claimed much of its territory.
question.clue: This conflict began with the invasion of the Mato Grosso province.

swap.leadin: He employed the Caravan of Death, authorized Operation Colombo, and relied on the economic advice of the Chicago Boys.
swap.text: Name this Chilean dictator from 1973 to 1990 who discarded the Alessandri constitution and was replaced as leader by Patricio Aylwin.
swap.clue: The Shock Doctrine outlined this leader's economic policies, shaped by the "Chicago Boys."

question.leadin: While staying on this island, one leader was warned of an attempted assassination by Jose Antonio Paez.
question.text: Name this island which titles an 1815 "Letter" advocating for Latin American unity. Earlier, this island was the site of Maroon revolts led by Nanny and Cudjoe.
question.clue: Simon Bolivar advocated for a united Latin America in a letter from this island, where he was exiled to in 1815.

swap.text: In the 1980s, a group known as this city's "boys" directed the economic policies of Chile after studying in the United States.

question.text: An 18th-century rebel leader who took Tupac's name was in turn the namesake of the radical group which seized the Japanese embassy during the tenure of this president of Peru. This man of Japanese descent created death squads to combat the Shining Path insurgency.
question.clue: A paramilitary group supporting this leader, Grupo Colina, killed fifteen partygoers in the Barrios Altos massacre.

swap.leadin: Gary Webb resigned his job after writing Dark Alliance, a book about how this group caused the Los Angeles crack epidemic with the approval of the CIA.
swap.text: Name these anti-communist groups that include the FDN and MILPAS. These groups carried out numerous massacres of civilians in Central America in the 1980s.
swap.clue: National Security Decision Directive 17 targeted this group, which used the training manual Psychological Operations in Guerrilla Warfare.

question.leadin: Answer these questions on the Mexican war of independence.
question.text: Command of the Mexican Rebel forces was first under this man, who famously rallied support through his famous "Cry of Dolores" speech. He is considered the "Father of Mexico." He was captured and subsequently executed following the Battle of Calderon Bridge.
question.clue: During an 1810 Mass, this man denounced the new Spanish monarchy in the Grito de Dolores.

swap.text: In 1990s the Zapatistas frequently clashed with Mexican paramilitary forces in this state, where one can find the Mayan ruins of Palenque. It shares its western border with Oaxaca.
swap.clue: The Chan Muan stele is found at ruins in this state, which is home to another site that includes the Temple of the Inscriptions.

question.leadin: A liberal party with this name instituted divorce rights and an eight-hour workday during the "First Batllismo" ("bah-CHEEZ-moh"), which Howard Wiarda identified as a precursor of Latin American populism.
question.text: Give this name of a party that held power in Uruguay from 1865 to 1958 despite its "coparticipacion" ("koh-par-tee-see-pah-S'YOAN") with the Blancos. Alfredo Stroessner ("ess-TROZE-nair") led a conservative party with this name that controlled Paraguay after the War of the Triple Alliance.
question.answerHtml: Colorado Party [or Colorados or PC or Partido Colorado; accept Red Party; accept National Republican Association – Colorado Party or Asociación Nacional Republicana – Partido Colorado or ANR-PC; prompt on Republican Party or Partido Republicano]
question.clue: This party, once led by Jose Batlle (BAT-zhay), controlled a capital city that was besieged by Manuel Oribe for nine years during a civil war called the "Guerra Grande."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a South American ruler.
swap.text: This second and final Brazilian emperor skillfully played his country's liberal and conservative factions against one another to rule for most of his 1831 to 1889 reign with near absolute power.
swap.clue: Events during his reign included the socialist Praieira revolt, and the Platine War, where he defeated Manuel Oribe and Juan Manuel de Rosas.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the popular historical pastime of gun-running.
question.text: Salvador Allende's already-dicey position in Chile was damaged even further by this scandal, in which the namesake containers delivered by aircraft from a friendly regime were discovered to be filled with grenades and machine guns.

swap.text: The song "Mulher Rendeira" is like a corrido; however, instead of praising a hero of the Mexican revolution it was written in honor of this cangaceiro. Eric Hobsbawm listed this Brazilian folk hero alongside Villa and Ned Kelly as an example of what he termed "social bandits."
swap.clue: This man and his followers used a long, thin knife nicknamed a "fish-filleter."

question.leadin: Answer the following about the quilombo communities of Brazil.
question.text: This most powerful quilombo, sometimes called Angola Janga, had a fortress at Macaco in the state of Alagoas and held out against the Portuguese until 1694, when it was taken over by Bernardo de Melo and others.
question.clue: Escaped Brazilian slaves lived in cities called quilombos, with this city ruled by Ganga Zumba is normally credited as the largest. Treasure seeking bandeirantes from Sao Paulo conquered this city in 1694.

swap.text: The Paraguayan forces were led by this general, who later served as Paraguayan president before being killed in a 1940 air crash. He drove Paraguayan forces into Bolivian territory, where the war stalled.

question.text: This man succeeded Mitre as the President of Argentina in 1868, and is best known for policies promoting education. He also wrote Facundo.

swap.leadin: A general from this modern country legendarily shouted "about face!" ordering his retreating men to turn and charge the pursuing Spanish calvary at the Battle of Las Queseras del Medio.
swap.text: Identify this country home to that mythologically nicknamed general, who led both this country's independence from Spain and La Cosiata, the movement which separated it from a larger post-colonial state.
swap.answerHtml: Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela [or República Bolivariana de Venezuela] (José Antonio Páez was nicknamed the “Centaur of the Plains.”)
swap.clue: From 1945 to 1948, it was led by the Democratic Action party in a period called "El Trienio Adeco."
